- Out-of-sample period: 2009-09-08 to 2026-09-30
- Data downloaded (UTC): 2026-10-11 19:50 to 2026-10-11 21:09
- Baseline design: 504 trading days in-sample, 252 out-of-sample, weight cap 5%, trades 1 day after the optimisation, costs 10 bp per unit traded
- DR = diversification ratio. Returns are in USD

### Data check: why the backtest starts on 2009-09-04

| Date | Index members | With prices | Without prices | Coverage |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2008-12-02 | 500 | 462 | 38 | 92.4% |
| 2009-03-05 | 500 | 471 | 29 | 94.2% |
| 2009-06-04 | 499 | 473 | 26 | 94.8% |
| 2009-09-02 | 500 | 474 | 26 | 94.8% |
| 2009-09-04 | 500 | 475 | 25 | 95.0% |

Prices of delisted companies start on 2006-11-30, so the first date with a full in-sample window of 504 days is 2008-12-02. The backtest starts on the first date from which at least 95% of the index members have prices on every trading day until the end of the sample. The last day below that level is 2009-09-03. The members without prices are companies that no longer trade and for which no free price history was found; most of the ones missing at the earliest dates stopped trading before mid-2009.

195 companies that no longer trade were in the index during the backtest and have prices from bolsamania.com (listed in t0d_delisted.csv). That source has holes: days on which the stock traded but the page has no price, mostly in 2022 and 2023. During a hole the stock is moved with the S&P 500 fund and the day its price returns takes the rest of the move, so the return over the hole is the true one (see `bridge` in maxdiv/data_prep.py). Ordinary cash dividends of these companies are not included because no free source has them, so their return is understated.

### Walk-forward: diversification ratio in-sample and out-of-sample

| Portfolio | Windows | DR in-sample (average) | DR out-of-sample (average) | Walk-forward efficiency (out / in) | Lowest DR out-of-sample | Highest DR out-of-sample | DR in-sample, in blocks | Efficiency, like for like |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Most Diversified Portfolio | 17 | 2.62 | 2.36 | 90% | 1.54 | 3.28 | 2.63 | 90% |
| Minimum variance | 17 | 2.10 | 2.01 | 96% | 1.40 | 3.13 | 2.12 | 95% |
| Equal weight | 17 | 1.70 | 1.86 | 109% | 1.35 | 2.93 | 1.75 | 106% |

Each window: weights fitted on 504 trading days, then held for the next 252. Both DR columns use the plain sample covariance of the window they refer to and the weights set at the start of the out-of-sample window. All three portfolios use the same eligible stocks. The last, incomplete window is excluded. 'In blocks': the in-sample window is cut into consecutive blocks of 252 days and the DR of each block is averaged, so that in-sample and out-of-sample are measured over the same horizon; 'like for like' divides the out-of-sample DR by it.

### Out-of-sample performance, after trading costs

| Portfolio | Return per year | Before costs | Volatility | Sharpe ratio | Worst drawdown | Beta to SPY | Turnover per year | Stocks held | Share that no longer trades |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Most Diversified Portfolio | 10.8% | 11.0% | 14.7% | 0.68 | -33.5% | 0.73 | 56% | 45 | 4.3% |
| Minimum variance | 11.0% | 11.1% | 12.7% | 0.77 | -34.2% | 0.59 | 51% | 43 | 2.1% |
| Equal weight | 12.8% | 12.9% | 17.5% | 0.69 | -38.7% | 0.98 | 12% | 488 | 0.8% |

| S&P 500 Equal Weight ETF (RSP) | 12.7% | – | 17.8% | 0.68 | -39.0% | 1.00 | – | – | – |

2009-09-09 to 2026-09-30. Costs: 10 bp of every dollar bought or sold. Turnover is one-way (100% = the whole portfolio replaced once a year). Sharpe ratio over 3-month Treasury bill (DTB3). SPY is the S&P 500 cap-weighted ETF; RSP is the S&P 500 Equal Weight ETF. 'Share that no longer trades': part of the portfolio that, on an average day, is in a company that has stopped trading (the cash of a takeover, mostly). It stays at its last price, earning nothing, until the next rebalance.

### Where the volatility comes from: the stocks held and how they are combined

| Portfolio | Average volatility of the stocks held | Diversification ratio | Volatility of the portfolio |
|---|---|---|---|
| Most Diversified Portfolio | 31.3% | 2.36 | 13.9% |
| Minimum variance | 22.3% | 2.01 | 11.6% |
| Equal weight | 29.2% | 1.86 | 16.5% |

Averages of the out-of-sample windows (the volatility of a window is lower than that of the whole period, which also has the changes from one window to the next). The volatility of a portfolio is the average volatility of its stocks divided by its diversification ratio. The MDP divides by the largest number, but it starts from stocks that are more volatile than the average; minimum variance starts from the calm ones.

### Survivorship bias: the same backtest without the companies that later disappeared

| Portfolio | Return per year, all index members | Return per year, survivors only | Survivorship bias (points per year) | Sharpe, all members | Sharpe, survivors only | Average weight in companies that later disappeared | Highest |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Most Diversified Portfolio | 10.8% | 10.4% | -0.4 | 0.68 | 0.62 | 22.9% | 49.8% |
| Equal weight | 12.8% | 13.6% | +0.8 | 0.69 | 0.73 | 13.9% | 29.1% |

'Survivors only' repeats the walk-forward run using, at each date, only the index members that are still listed today. That is the universe available from a source that deletes delisted companies, such as Yahoo Finance. The difference between the two columns is the survivorship bias.

### Sharpe ratio: portfolios that are not chosen with hindsight

| Portfolio | Return per year | Volatility | Sharpe ratio | Worst drawdown | Turnover per year | Sharpe minus baseline (95% interval) | Sharpe minus SPY (95% interval) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Baseline MDP | 10.8% | 14.7% | 0.68 | -33.5% | 56% | – | -0.12 (-0.37 to +0.13) |
| Average of the 6 versions of the MDP | 11.5% | 14.3% | 0.73 | -31.7% | 52% | +0.05 (+0.00 to +0.11) | -0.07 (-0.31 to +0.17) |
| Best of the 6 versions of the MDP so far | 12.2% | 14.6% | 0.76 | -32.2% | 50% | +0.08 (+0.01 to +0.15) | -0.04 (-0.30 to +0.22) |
| Best of 18 candidates so far (MDP to minimum variance) | 10.2% | 14.4% | 0.64 | -34.2% | 60% | -0.03 (-0.19 to +0.13) | -0.15 (-0.42 to +0.12) |
| S&P 500 ETF (SPY) | 14.5% | 17.0% | 0.80 | -33.7% | – | +0.12 (-0.13 to +0.37) | – |

'Average': the mean of the weights of the versions of the MDP (three in-sample windows, two shrinkage targets); nothing is chosen. 'Best so far': on each optimisation date, the candidate with the highest Sharpe ratio on its own out-of-sample returns up to that day; the first 3 years hold the baseline. The last two rows repeat the baseline and the choice between versions of the MDP giving the delisted companies the dividends that their prices lack (an assumption, see t5b); their 'minus baseline' is against the baseline with the same dividends. Interval above 0: Average of the 6 versions of the MDP; Best of the 6 versions of the MDP so far; Best of the 6 versions of the MDP so far + 2% dividend for the delisted companies. Several portfolios are compared with the baseline, so an interval that only just leaves 0 out is weak evidence.
